questions.title: Animal Dog Speak Override
questions.description:
Drill: single inheritance with an overridden method.
Write class Animal with a method speak() that returns 'Some generic sound'. Write class Dog(Animal) whose constructor stores a sound word and whose speak() method returns that word, overriding the parent version.

Input Format:
One line: the dog's sound (may contain spaces)

Output Format:
Line 1: result of Animal().speak()
Line 2: result of Dog(sound).speak()

Constraints:
1 <= len(sound) <= 20

questions.title: Phone Inherits Device Brand
questions.description:
Drill: a child object inherits attributes initialised by the parent constructor.
Write class Device whose constructor stores a brand. Write class Phone(Device) whose constructor receives brand and model, passes brand up to the parent constructor, and stores model itself.

Input Format:
Line 1: brand (may contain spaces)
Line 2: model (may contain spaces)

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Brand: <brand>' (attribute inherited from Device)
Line 2: 'Model: <model>' (attribute owned by Phone)

Constraints:
1 <= len(brand), len(model) <= 30

questions.title: Team Banner Grandparent Method
questions.description:
Drill: multilevel inheritance chain Organization -> Department -> Team. The Team object calls a method defined on its grandparent class, using an attribute set two levels up.
class Organization stores a name. class Department(Organization) adds nothing. class Team(Department) defines banner() returning 'Team belongs to <name>'.

Input Format:
One line: the organization name (may contain spaces)

Output Format:
Print the string returned by Team(name).banner().

Constraints:
1 <= len(name) <= 40

questions.title: Parrot Penguin Same Parent
questions.description:
Drill: hierarchical inheritance — two child classes of one parent, each with its own method.
class Bird stores a name. class Parrot(Bird) defines move() returning '<name> flies high'. class Penguin(Bird) defines move() returning '<name> swims deep'.

Input Format:
One line: the bird's name (may contain spaces)

Output Format:
Line 1: Parrot(name).move()
Line 2: Penguin(name).move()

Constraints:
1 <= len(name) <= 20
questions.sampleoutput1:
Rio flies high
Rio swims deep
questions.sampleoutput2:
Pip flies high
Pip swims deep
questions.output1:
Sky flies high
Sky swims deep
questions.output2:
Waddle flies high
Waddle swims deep
questions.output3:
Kiwi flies high
Kiwi swims deep

questions.title: Savings Account Extra Rate
questions.description:
Drill: a child constructor that extends the parent constructor with one extra attribute.
class Account stores owner and balance. class SavingsAccount(Account) also stores an interest rate, calling the parent constructor first with super().__init__(owner, balance).

Input Format:
One line: owner balance rate (space separated; owner is one word, balance and rate are integers)

Output Format:
Print '<owner> has <balance> at <rate>% interest' using the object's three attributes.

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 1000000 and 1 <= rate <= 12

questions.title: Textbook Inherited Shelf Method
questions.description:
Drill: a child object calls a method it never defined — it is inherited, and the method reads an attribute the child added.
class Book stores a title and defines shelf() returning '<title> on shelf'. class Textbook(Book) additionally stores a subject and does NOT redefine shelf().

Input Format:
Line 1: title (may contain spaces)
Line 2: subject (may contain spaces)

Output Format:
Line 1: result of calling the inherited shelf() on a Textbook object
Line 2: the subject attribute

Constraints:
1 <= len(title), len(subject) <= 30
questions.output1:
Intro to Python on shelf
Computer Science

questions.title: School Role Based Intros
questions.description:
A school intranet prints a one-line introduction for each staff member, and the wording depends on the role.
Write class Staff whose constructor stores the name. Write class Teacher(Staff) that also stores a subject with intro() returning 'Teacher <name> teaches <subject>'. Write class Principal(Staff) that also stores years of service with intro() returning 'Principal <name> with <years> years of service'.

Input Format:
Line 1: role, exactly TEACHER or PRINCIPAL
Line 2: name (may contain spaces)
Line 3: subject for a teacher, or years of service (integer) for a principal

Output Format:
Print the intro() string of the matching child object.

Constraints:
role is TEACHER or PRINCIPAL, 1 <= len(name), len(subject) <= 30 and 1 <= years <= 40
questions.sampleoutput2: Principal Mr. Rao with 15 years of service
questions.output2: Principal Ms. Iyer with 22 years of service
questions.inputconstrains: role is TEACHER or PRINCIPAL, 1 <= years <= 40

questions.title: Bike Car Rent Factors
questions.description:
A rental shop prices vehicles from a per-day rate and a class-wide pricing factor: bikes get a 10 percent discount (factor 0.9) and cars carry a 15 percent surge (factor 1.15). The rent formula itself lives once on the parent class and reads the factor from the current object.
Write class Vehicle with a class attribute factor = 1.0, a constructor storing rate, and a method rent(days) returning rate * days * self.factor. Write class Bike(Vehicle) with factor = 0.9 and class Car(Vehicle) with factor = 1.15.

Input Format:
One line: kind rate days (space separated; kind is BIKE or CAR, rate and days are integers)

Output Format:
Print the rent with exactly two decimal places.

Constraints:
kind is BIKE or CAR, 1 <= rate <= 5000 and 1 <= days <= 30
questions.inputconstrains: kind is BIKE or CAR, 1 <= rate <= 5000, 1 <= days <= 30

questions.title: Smart Fridge Three Level Status
questions.description:
A kitchen appliance app models a smart fridge with a three-level chain: Appliance -> Fridge -> SmartFridge.
class Appliance stores the brand. class Fridge(Appliance) also stores the capacity in litres. class SmartFridge(Fridge) also stores the target temperature and defines status() returning '<brand> fridge <capacity>L cooling to <temp>C'.

Input Format:
One line: brand capacity temp (space separated; brand is one word, capacity and temp are integers)

Output Format:
Print the status() string of the SmartFridge object.

Constraints:
50 <= capacity <= 800 and 1 <= temp <= 9

questions.title: Square Cube Chain Metrics
questions.description:
A geometry app models solids with a multilevel chain: Shape -> Square -> Cube.
class Shape stores the side length. class Square(Shape) defines area() returning side * side. class Cube(Square) defines volume() returning side raised to the power 3.

Input Format:
One line: the side length (integer)

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Area: <area>' computed by the Square method
Line 2: 'Volume: <volume>' computed by the Cube method

Constraints:
1 <= side <= 1000

questions.title: Manager Pay Accumulation Chain
questions.description:
A company models managers with a three-level chain Person -> Employee -> Manager, where each level initialises one more attribute through super() calls.
class Person stores the name. class Employee(Person) also stores the base salary. class Manager(Employee) also stores the bonus and defines total() returning base + bonus.

Input Format:
One line: name base bonus (space separated; name is one word, base and bonus are integers)

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Name: <name>' (set by Person)
Line 2: 'Base: <base>' (set by Employee)
Line 3: 'Total: <total>' (computed by Manager)

Constraints:
0 <= base, bonus <= 200000 and name is one word

questions.title: Copier Mixin Behaviour
questions.description:
An office machine combines two behaviours through multiple inheritance: Printer knows how to print a document and Scanner knows how to scan one, while Copier inherits from both and adds a copy method.
class Printer defines print_doc(doc) returning 'Printing <doc>'. class Scanner defines scan_doc(doc) returning 'Scanning <doc>'. class Copier(Printer, Scanner) defines copy(doc) returning 'Copy of <doc> ready'.

Input Format:
One line: doc mode (space separated; doc is one word, mode is PRINT, SCAN or COPY)

Output Format:
PRINT: print_doc(doc) only.
SCAN: scan_doc(doc) only.
COPY: print_doc(doc), then scan_doc(doc), then copy(doc) — three lines in that order.

Constraints:
mode is PRINT, SCAN or COPY and 1 <= len(doc) <= 40
questions.sampleoutput1:
Printing report.pdf
Scanning report.pdf
Copy of report.pdf ready
questions.output2:
Printing photo.png
Scanning photo.png
Copy of photo.png ready
questions.inputconstrains: mode is PRINT, SCAN or COPY, 1 <= len(doc) <= 40

questions.title: Diamond Label Resolution Pick
questions.description:
Three classes define the same method info(), and a fourth class inherits from two of them. Which info() runs is decided by the method resolution order.
class A defines info() returning self.lab. class B(A) and class C(A) each override info() the same way (returning self.lab), and class D(B, C) defines nothing extra. Each class has a class attribute lab, and the driver assigns the three input labels to A.lab, B.lab and C.lab before instantiating.

Input Format:
One line: three space-separated labels for A, B and C

Output Format:
Line 1: D().info()
Line 2: C().info()
Line 3: A().info()

Constraints:
3 labels, each 1 <= len <= 15

questions.title: Notification Channel Dispatch
questions.description:
An alert console dispatches events over two channels built on one base class: EmailNotification and SMSNotification both extend Notification and each formats its message differently.
class Notification stores the message. class EmailNotification(Notification) defines send() returning 'EMAIL: <message>'. class SMSNotification(Notification) defines send() returning 'SMS: <message>'.

Input Format:
Line 1: number of events n
Next n lines: channel and message (channel is EMAIL or SMS; the message may contain spaces and runs to the end of the line)

Output Format:
One line per event in input order: the string returned by the matching child's send().

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, channel is EMAIL or SMS and 1 <= len(message) <= 80
questions.sampleinput1:
3
EMAIL Server down
SMS OTP 4482
EMAIL Weekly digest
questions.sampleoutput1:
EMAIL: Server down
SMS: OTP 4482
EMAIL: Weekly digest
questions.input1:
2
EMAIL Invoice attached
SMS Balance low
questions.output1:
EMAIL: Invoice attached
SMS: Balance low
questions.input2:
4
SMS A
EMAIL B
SMS C
EMAIL D
questions.output2:
SMS: A
EMAIL: B
SMS: C
EMAIL: D
questions.input3:
2
EMAIL Meeting at 5
SMS Call me
questions.output3:
EMAIL: Meeting at 5
SMS: Call me
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50, channel is EMAIL or SMS

questions.title: Science Student Practical Totals
questions.description:
A school computes a science student's grand total as theory marks plus practical marks. Regular students have only theory marks, so the base class totals the theory list; the science subclass extends the total with the practical list on top of the parent's result.
class Student stores name and a theory list with a method total() that loops over the theory marks. class ScienceStudent(Student) additionally stores a practical list and overrides total() to return super().total() plus the sum of the practical marks accumulated in a loop.

Input Format:
Line 1: name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: theory marks (space-separated integers)
Line 3: practical marks (space-separated integers)

Output Format:
Print '<name>: <grand total>'.

Constraints:
at least 1 mark per line and 0 <= mark <= 100
questions.inputconstrains: 0 <= mark <= 100, at least 1 mark per line

questions.title: Member Tier Point Multipliers
questions.description:
A loyalty programme multiplies earned points by membership tier: GOLD members earn double points (factor 2) and SILVER members earn 1.5 times their points.
class Member stores the name and points with a method earn() returning the points unchanged. class GoldMember(Member) overrides earn() returning points * 2. class SilverMember(Member) overrides earn() returning points * 1.5.

Input Format:
Line 1: number of members n
Next n lines: tier name points (space separated; tier is GOLD or SILVER, points is an integer)

Output Format:
One line per member in input order: '<name> earns <points earned>' with two decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, tier is GOLD or SILVER and 0 <= points <= 100000

3
GOLD Asha 100
SILVER Bala 80
GOLD Chetan 50
questions.sampleoutput1:
Asha earns 200.00
Bala earns 120.00
Chetan earns 100.00
questions.input2:
3
SILVER Gita 6
GOLD Hari 25
GOLD Iman 12
questions.output2:
Gita earns 9.00
Hari earns 50.00
Iman earns 24.00

questions.title: Diamond MRO Value Engine
questions.description:
A value-resolution engine demonstrates a diamond: class Base stores a value v. class Left(Base) overrides describe() returning 'Left <v + 10>' and initialises v through an explicit Base.__init__(self, v) call. class Right(Base) overrides describe() returning 'Right <v * 2>'. class Child(Left, Right) adds nothing. Python resolves Child's describe through the MRO, which the engine prints as a class-name chain.

Input Format:
One line: the integer value v

Output Format:
Line 1: Child(v).describe()
Line 2: Right(v + 1).describe()
Line 3: the MRO of Child as class names joined with ' -> '

Constraints:
-100 <= v <= 100
questions.sampleoutput1:
Left 15
Right 12
Child -> Left -> Right -> Base -> object
questions.sampleoutput2:
Left 10
Right 2
Child -> Left -> Right -> Base -> object
questions.output1:
Left 7
Right -4
Child -> Left -> Right -> Base -> object
questions.output2:
Left 110
Right 202
Child -> Left -> Right -> Base -> object
questions.output3:
Left 60
Right 102
Child -> Left -> Right -> Base -> object

questions.title: Multilevel Bill Tax Stacking
questions.description:
A billing engine stacks charges through a three-level chain: Bill -> TaxedBill -> FinalBill. The grandparent totals the plain amount, the parent adds 18 percent tax by overriding total(), and the child adds a delivery fee on top of the parent's total using an explicit TaxedBill.total(self) call (no super()).

Input Format:
Line 1: number of bills n and the delivery fee (space separated; fee may be fractional)
Next n lines: one bill amount each (may be fractional)

Output Format:
For each bill, two lines in order: 'Taxed: <amount * 1.18>' and 'Final: <taxed + fee>', each with two decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 0 <= fee <= 1000 and 0 <= amount <= 100000
questions.output1:
Taxed: 118.00
Final: 138.00
Taxed: 0.00
Final: 20.00
Taxed: 1178.82
Final: 1198.82

questions.title: Hospital Staff Salary Gates
questions.description:
A hospital payroll gate computes pay per role from a base salary: doctors earn base * 3 + 500, nurses earn base * 1.5 + 100 and receptionists earn base + 200. Any other role string is not on the payroll gate.
Write class Staff storing name and base. Write three child classes Doctor, Nurse and Receptionist, each with a pay() method applying its role formula. Read staff records in a loop, instantiate the correct child (with an if/elif chain, no dictionary dispatch), and handle unknown roles.

Input Format:
Line 1: number of staff records n
Next n lines: role name base (space separated; base is an integer, name is one word)

Output Format:
One line per record in input order: '<name>: <pay>' with two decimal places, or '<name>: UNKNOWN ROLE' when the role is not DOCTOR, NURSE or RECEPTIONIST.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= base <= 100000 and name is one word
questions.sampleinput1:
3
DOCTOR Rao 1000
NURSE Sneha 800
RECEPTIONIST Sam 500
questions.input1:
4
NURSE B1 0
DOCTOR C1 2000
RECEPTIONIST D1 0
VOLUNTEER E1 100
questions.input3:
3
DOCTOR H1 3333
NURSE I1 2222
CHAPLAIN J1 100

questions.title: Mage Upgrade Attack Stacking
questions.description:
A strategy game stacks attack power through a multilevel upgrade chain: Unit -> Mage -> Archmage. A unit attacks with its raw power; a mage adds twice the spell power; an archmage adds the staff bonus on top of the mage formula, calling Mage.attack(self) explicitly (no super()).

Input Format:
One line: name power spell staff (space separated; name is one word, the rest are integers)

Output Format:
Build Unit(name, power), Mage(name, power, spell) and Archmage(name, power, spell, staff), then print:
Line 1: 'Unit <unit attack>'
Line 2: 'Mage <mage attack>'
Line 3: 'Archmage <archmage attack>'

Constraints:
0 <= power, spell, staff <= 1000 and 1 <= len(name) <= 20
